exposure: Maternal exposure to selective antidepressants (SADs) during pregnancy
cohort: The study included infants exposed to selective antidepressants during pregnancy (some with and some without poor neonatal adaptation) and infants not exposed to selective antidepressants (controls).
finding: Infants with poor neonatal adaptation (PNA) had higher hair cortisol levels compared to infants without PNA, a difference that was statistically significant only in female infants.
